notes: Access: reached directly with curl_cffi impersonate=chrome (desktop Chrome TLS fingerprint), consistent with the prior Furniture-pass note for this host; no block encountered on any of the ~20 URLs fetched this session. robots.txt has no Claude/Anthropic-named disallow (checked first). Navigation discovery: homepage mega-nav 'Best Sellers' top-level link -> https://www.perigold.com/curated/shop-all-best-sellers~ev445166.html (a genuine BrowseGrid PLP with pagination, browseResultCount JSON field = 1739, matching the page's own visible '1,739 Items' header). Site search (keyword.php?keyword=best+sellers) redirects to https://www.perigold.com/m/best-sellers, which is a curated landing/hub page (title 'Perigold | Best Sellers') composed of per-department carousels (no single BrowseGrid/count of its own) that link out to 8 department-specific 'Bestselling <Department>' listing pages found in the same nav dropdown: Furniture, Decor, Dining & Entertaining, Home Renovation, Lighting, Outdoor, Rugs, Bed & Bath. Each of these 8 was opened directly; all are real paginated BrowseGrid PLPs with their own browseResultCount matching their visible '<N> Items' header exactly. These department counts do not sum to or nest inside the 1739 'Shop All' figure (they range 364-4249 each, summing far higher), so they are genuinely separate curated selections under the same Best Sellers umbrella rather than a strict parent/children partition - kept as independent sibling rows per the brief's 'multiple PLPs, genuinely different listings -> keep both' rule, not as a null-qty grouping parent, since every row here has its own exact, verifiable count. Also checked sitemap (seo-category-sitemap~0.xml) which has no bestseller-named nodes (expected - these are merchandising/curated pages, not category taxonomy) and confirms no other bestseller variants exist outside the nav-discovered set. No individual-PDP 'Bestseller' badges were treated as PLPs.
